title: Handshake Metadata Federation Proposal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a lightweight federation layer for handshake metadata between client SDKs (edge) and any Redwood Inference deployment variant (hosted, dedicated, private). Motivation: multiple products need richer session metadata at connection time (client capabilities, privacy tags, preferred routing hints) but we want a pluggable, versioned, auditable mechanism that doesn’t bloat per-request payloads and can be validated/policed by platform operators.

Goals:
- Define a compact, extensible "handshake metadata" API shape for initial session establishment (not per request).
- Support federated metadata providers so different orgs (or middleboxes) can append/endorse metadata without full trust.
- Enable validation and policy enforcement at ingress (rate limits, routing decisions, privacy filters).
- Make the shape forward/backwards-compatible and easy to roll out from SDKs.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for per-request attribution (tokens, api keys).
- Not intended to carry bulk context or user PII by default.

High-level flow (negotiation):
1) Client opens session (WebSocket/HTTP2/initial REST). Sends a compact metadata envelope as part of the handshake.
2) Ingress validates envelope signature(s) and canonicalizes claims to a session metadata blob.
3) Metadata is stored (ephemeral or persisted depending on policy) and referenced by session-id.
4) Routing/authorization policies consult session metadata.
5) Metadata provider federation: optional additional endorsements can be fetched or attached by the client or by a trusted sidecar.

API shape (compact example):
---
{
  "v": "1",                     // version string, semantic minor for additions
  "sid": "s-1234abcd",         // client-supplied session id (optional)
  "caps": ["streaming","embeddings"], // client capabilities
  "privacy": ["no-logs"],      // privacy tags (policy-readable)
  "hints": {"region": "eu-west-1"}, // routing hints (best-effort)
  "providers": [                  // optional appended metadata providers
    {
      "id": "org:partner-a",
      "sig": "base64sig...",
      "claims": "eyJjbHVzIjpbImF1dGgiXX0"  // base64-encoded JSON claims (compact)
    }
  ]
}
---
Notes on the shape:
- Keep it small. "claims" can be base64-encoded to avoid nested JSON in the top-level frame.
- "providers" is ordered; the first trusted provider wins on conflicting scalar claims unless policy says merge.
- "v" supports inexpensive compatibility checks at ingress before parsing further.

Federation model options (sketches):
A) Client-attached endorsements: SDKs carry endorsements from third-party attestors (e.g., MNOs, partners). Ingress verifies signatures against configured roots. Pros: low-latency, client-driven. Cons: key distribution/trust list complexity.
B) Sidecar/Proxy enrichment: An enterprise sidecar adds organization-specific claims and signs them. Good for private deployments.
C) On-demand provider fetch: Ingress can call an external registry to validate or fetch endorsements for the client-ident (higher latency).

Policy & enforcement examples:
- If privacy tag includes "no-logs", disallow persistence of user-provided text under that session.
- If hints.region != deployment.region and org policy forbids cross-region routing, return HTTP 403 at handshake.
- If providers contains an unrecognized signer, mark session as "untrusted" and restrict CPU-bound models.

Storage model:
- Ephemeral: store session metadata in an in-memory cache keyed by session-id for <= 24h. Good for hosted/dedicated.
- Persistent: write to short-lived DB row for auditing (if policy allows). Private deployments may prefer persistent audit logs.

SDK ergonomics (JS/Go examples as pseudo):
- JS: RedwoodClient.openSession({metadata:{v:"1",caps:["chat"],privacy:["no-logs"]}})
- SDK will pack+sign if a local attestor key is present.

Compatibility & rollout:
- Start with v=1 with limited claims (caps, privacy, hints, sid).
- Admit unknown fields in ingress with a WARNING log and drop them unless operator opts-in.
- Provide a compatibility endpoint: /handshake/compat?v=1 -> returns allowed schema and sample.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Default deny for any privacy-claim-sensitive storage. Operators must opt-in to storing PII from claims.
- Signatures: prefer ed25519 for low-compute verification. Signature cover: canonicalized claim bytes + metadata version + issuer id.
- Replay: include a client-supplied nonce + server timestamp in signed payloads to limit replay.

Operational notes:
- Add a lightweight schema validator in the ingress path to avoid full JSON parsing on malformed frames.
- Expose debugging header X-Session-Meta-Status with values (ok/warn/untrusted) for quick dev feedback in logs.

Open questions / next steps:
- Governed trust roots: where do operator-managed signer public keys live? (k8s secrets? external key registry?)
- Rate of change for provider list & revocation process.
- How to surface provider trust decisions in Redwood Console so customers can see why a session was routed/restricted.
- Performance baseline: define max handshake envelope size (e.g., 2KB) and benchmark verification cost per CPU-core.

TODOs:
- Prototype: ingress validator + small SDK helper to emit v=1 envelopes (owner: Ava).
- Add integration test asserting privacy tag enforcement (owner: Sofia).
- Draft console UI mock for per-session metadata inspector (owner: Liam).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep claims deliberately minimal. If we need richer capability descriptors, add a separate capability registry keyed by short ids to avoid bloat.
- Consider a future "handshake delta" mechanism to allow clients to append claims mid-session without re-opening sockets.

End.
